purpose: Editorially selected Signals candidates for the Sunday 4 October 2026 edition. Selections favour primary-source developments with a concrete control, custody, enforcement, or governance decision; quiet topics retain reviewed anchors rather than promote thin items.

topics.editorialRationale: Select OpenAI's case study of Chatham's transaction-validation workflow because it compares system records with client-authorised and executed terms, flags discrepancies, and is still being checked against experienced reviewers before automation expands. Treat the performance claims as supplier-reported.

Select the SEC's proposed crypto-asset custody framework because self-custody and state trust-company pathways would change the control and counterparty choices available to advisers and regulated funds. Label it clearly as a proposal open for comment, not an adopted rule.

No new provider incident adds sufficiently corroborated decision value this week. Retain the reviewed dependency and supervision evidence; do not elevate a single-provider status notice merely to create a fresh item.

The available notices are isolated service-status reports without enough independent evidence or broader control implications. Retain the reviewed resilience anchor rather than promote a weak item to fill coverage.

Select the NCA report of a court confiscation order and continuing restrictions on finances and business interests because it illustrates post-conviction asset recovery and prevention controls. Keep the item specific to this case; it does not establish a general enforcement trend.

Select distinct, source-supported cyber signals rather than repeating weekly KEV notices: Canada's 27 September Citrix alert, updated 3 October, describes active exploitation and gateway containment; Microsoft reports exploitation of a Zimbra command-injection flaw and gives a patch/mitigation path; Rapid7's 2 October research details BPFDoor and AVERAT activity against network-edge devices; and CISA's 2 October KEV addition remains a separate remediation trigger. Preserve publication and update dates accurately and distinguish advisory, threat-research and catalog evidence.

The fresh outage candidate is a single vendor's status notice and does not add enough corroborated decision value beyond the retained dependency record. Keep the reviewed technology-failure anchor rather than manufacture a new theme.

Select the Irish DPC's final decision summary because it links physical paper-record handling and confidential-waste controls to GDPR security duties, a reprimand, and required DPIAs and remediation. The DPC says the full decision will follow, so describe only the published summary.
